prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create actual newly illustrated 2D game animation frame artwork, not a preview board. The supplied PNG is the approved character design and painting style reference, not an image to rotate, scale, squash, warp or reuse as a cutout. Draw every pose afresh with coherent anatomy, newly drawn contours, material surfaces and lighting appropriate to that pose. Polished soft hand-painted 2D sprite shading, fine dark teal outline, warm upper-left light, exactly match the reference palette and visual finish. One sprite sheet only: exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, 16 equal square cells, read left to right then top to bottom. Requested output 2048x2048 pixels. Genuinely transparent background, NO checkerboard drawing, NO scene, ground, backdrop, shadows, labels, letters, numbers, grid lines, cell borders, glow or extra characters. No object crosses its cell boundary. Fixed camera, fixed drawing scale and fixed ground baseline at 88% of each cell. On the first frame the character is centered horizontally, full neutral visible height about 60% of a cell, from 28% to 88%; keep its mass and scale consistent, let only the actual death action change its silhouette. This is a one-shot DEATH followed by still remains, never return to life. Design the intervening drawings as sequential animation poses, not sixteen unrelated variations. All 16 cells must contain the same recognizable character at successive moments of the action. Character: the reference ochre golden-brown round faceted pebble creature with two tiny matching pebble feet and two dark forest-green eyes. Preserve its broad single stone body, subtle irregular polygonal planes and painterly rock grain. Death action: it braces briefly, branching cracks appear through the actual stone, then breaks into FOUR large thick angular stone chunks, which tumble down into a short pile with one small final jostle. Redraw every broken surface with newly exposed lighter ochre irregular fracture faces and darker side planes, fully three-dimensional solid chunks. This must NOT look like a flat standing picture cut into puzzle pieces or rotated cutouts. Let the large pieces visibly turn to show new cut faces and lose the original outer silhouette. Row 1 frames 1-4: neutral standing, eyes droop, a tense held pose, a first small branching crack opens from the top center. Row 2 frames 5-8: three branching cracks grow, eyes close and disappear as the seams open, rock splits into four solid volumes, upper chunks begin falling and turning. Row 3 frames 9-12: four heavy pieces visibly tumble with successive newly illustrated faces, land around the same ground position, settle into an irregular low rubble pile about half the initial height. Row 4 frames 13-16: one small heavy bounce/jostle, chunks clunk together and completely rest. Final row has four recognizable large stone chunks in a clear asymmetric rubble pile with broad new fracture surfaces, NOT a split oval still standing and NOT an empty gap in an unbroken body. Feet remain as small stones by the base. No eyes on final rubble, no gore, particles, smoke, sparkles, or extra debris cloud. Action is weighty and rigid, never rubbery. Preserve the warm palette, dark teal fine contours and upper-left painting light.
